data.translation: Uncle Isho: Wine, all the people used to make it. All of us, we used to make it; everybody used to make it. He would bring grapes from his vineyards. We used to press them with our hands; some also pressed them in sacks. And we would put it in the jars and close the mouths of the jars. They would remain forty or fifty days; it would ferment well. We would open them and drink it. To this day I have wine at home, perhaps six or seven years old.

data.translation: Uncle Isho: They used to press the wine first, put it in the kettles and boil it, a boil or two. And after it cooled, they would put it in the jars and close the mouths of the jars so that it would ferment well and become very strong.
